note: The weekly loop's first challengers, from the research (20 Nov 2026): what the research was unsure of, ranked, alternating first-second and look tests.

candidates.test: the Short's first spoken sentence pairs the small cause with its scale ('One stuck rudder. Two minutes. A riverboat on its side.' / 'A fuel handle behind his shoulder. One small plane, into the sea.'), the toll stated once and plainly when the story has one, against the champion's question-first hook that keeps the toll out of the first line
candidates.why: Owner note on L-20261121-42 (22 Nov): the hook should say a small issue led to this many deaths, to make people curious about the rest. The breakouts agree: Inside Decoded's 1.91M Short opens 'In about a minute, a jet fell more than 26,000 feet' (subject at 0 s, figure spoken at 1 s); Athena_Explains' 7.4M names the 167 saved at 1 s; World explained's 2.56M puts the 27,000-ft fall in the title. Our two Shorts open on a plain question (v-20261121-42, 167 views so far) and a rudder line. An owner note asking to change the recipe goes to the top of its kind. The payoff figure still waits for the payoff: the hook gives the scale, not the reason. Judged on stayed to watch, from 8 Shorts a side

candidates.test: frame 1 shows the last recorded exchange from the official report's CVR or ATC transcript as on-screen transcript text on a thing in the place (a recorder readout, a radio log), silent for about a second, then the narrator names the cause; only for stories with a final report that publishes the transcript, never the narrator voicing the words, against the champion's spoken question-first hook
candidates.why: This week's biggest small-channel Shorts in the niche open on the crew's own words: khoj's 'What the Learjet Co-Pilot Told Her Captain' 208.8K on 533 subscribers (34 s) and 'Her father heard the final radio recording' 198.1K on 533 (32 s); Air Crash Rebuilt's 'Look Outside!' 108.5K on 103 (54 s) (market-data, 27 Nov). Those quote an open investigation, which our profile rules out, so the test uses only closed reports (Colgan 3407, Asiana 214, Air Canada 797), shown as transcript text as the profile requires. Our 5 Shorts with data open on a spoken question (59-77% viewed, 44-1,180 views).

candidates.test: frame 1 one beat BEFORE the failure (the jet cruising, the bridge standing) against the champion's frame 1 AT the failure
candidates.why: Fault Lines opens cruising with the date caption (1.94M); Major Disasters opens on a silent warning card; the comments reward suddenness. Unsure which holds better

candidates.test: voice only with hard silences between lines against the champion's breathing drone ~32 dB under
candidates.why: 3 of 4 references run no bed at all; our drone is our own upgrade, unmeasured on viewers

candidates.test: varied silences in the Short's narration: about 0.3 s between lines that run on, about 1.2 s before the line that turns the story (the cause or the payoff), the 2.6 s failure silence kept, against the champion's even ~0.65 s gap after every line
candidates.why: Our three Shorts (v-20261121-42, v-20261122-41, v-20261123-41, render.json voice timings) leave the same 0.58-0.68 s after every line except one 2.6 s failure silence, so the voice runs at one rhythm. The references measured in research/sound.md vary theirs: Athena's 7.4M Short 0.4-1.7 s, Plainly Difficult 0.5-0.9 s, Major Disasters 0.8 s with a 6.7 s card. Unsure: a longer pause can also lose a swiper, so it is a test on held after the hook, not a default. Built in renderer/timeline/build.py beat gaps, behind a flag

candidates.test: fast hook, then held shots: keep the champion's shot change about every 1-1.5 s for the first ~8 s, then hold each explanation shot 4-6 s (one shot size with a slow push or orbit, things still moving inside it and one live instrument such as altitude, water level or pressure ticking on a thing in the place), against the champion's even change about every 1.6 s for the whole Short
candidates.why: Our four Shorts change shot size at one even rhythm from start to end: v-20261121-42 33 sizes in 49 s, v-20261122-41 28 in 48 s, v-20261123-41 27 in 47 s, v-20261124-41 27 in 46 s (params.camera), about one every 1.6 s, 6-7 in the first 10 s. The references speed up the hook and then hold: Athena's 7.4M Short about ten cuts in the first 10 s, then 5-7 s 3D shots; Inside Decoded's 1.9M Learjet Short holds 7-20 s shots with a telemetry panel; World explained's 2.5M keeps one vertical-speed meter through every shot (research/sheets, sampled, so their cut counts are lower bounds). Lac-Megantic, our only Short with retention, holds 43% stayed but only 23% after the hook. Unsure: a held shot can also feel slow, so it is a test on held after the hook; the liveliness gate (no 4 s stretch with nothing moving) and three shot sizes per video still apply. Built in the director prompt's camera plan behind a flag

candidates.test: a 3-4 s silent date/warning card before the cold open against straight into the 3D cold open
candidates.why: 2 of 4 long references open on 6-7 s of silence over a card (sound.md)

candidates.test: the story's live instrument on screen through the whole reconstruction against only in the last 90 s
candidates.why: Inside Decoded and World explained keep a telemetry panel in every shot of their Shorts (1.9M, 2.6M); unmeasured on long videos

candidates.test: titles as a question ('Could Any Pilot Have Saved It?') against claim titles
candidates.why: comments ask questions; Flying for Money's question titles got 2.8M/3.1M

candidates.test: long videos of 10-11 min against the owner's 8-10 min
candidates.why: the scan's 10-15 min band has the best on-niche median (775 vs 285) and 16% hits; owner's call: only with the owner's OK (notification)

candidates.test: Short titles that put the event's own figure against its clock ('Jet Fell 27,000 Feet in 60 Seconds', 'Two Minutes Later It Hit a Cruise Boat') against the champion's plain question title
candidates.why: Sunday teardown, niche scan of 20 Nov: World explained's 2.56M (669x its 3.8K subs) and Inside Decoded's 1.91M (144x) both name a distance and a time in the title; Trace the Failure's best Shorts do too. Major Disasters' plain-question historic titles sit at 193-1,612. No stayed-to-watch data of ours yet (1 Short, published 21 Nov). The payoff figure must still wait for the payoff: the title figure is the clock, not the toll

candidates.test: promo Shorts of 60-90 s (the cause chain told in full) against the champion's 30-50 s
candidates.why: Sunday teardown: World explained's Shorts median 96 s and its three breakouts run 107-115 s (2.56M, 1.25M, 468K); Inside Decoded's median 73 s, breakouts 81-98 s; Trace the Failure's median 66 s. Major Disasters at 43-46 s has a 193-view median. The setup scan's best bands were 35-50 s and 20-35 s, so the evidence conflicts: test, don't adopt. Judged on stayed to watch; also note views per Short in the digest

candidates.test: the last beat before the loop states the story's most surprising fact on a thing in the place, against the champion's investigators' board that asks a comment question ('Hand brakes or the test: which should have stopped it?', 'The fast hit or the slow capsize: which surprised you more?')
candidates.why: Both Shorts with retention end on a 5-6 s question board and hold little to the end: end hold 31% (v-20261121-42) and 25% (v-20261122-41), held after the hook 27% and 21%. No single drop at the board passes 7%, so it is not a lesson: unsure whether the question costs watchers or earns comments (0 comments so far on either).

candidates.test: the promo's closing line as one sentence of about 2 s ('The full minute-by-minute is on the channel.') straight after the payoff, against the champion's 5-7 s loop beat that asks a comment question and then points to the channel
candidates.why: Titan v-20261125-41 lost 16.4% at 48.5 s inside its 7 s loop beat ('The company or the rules: who should have stopped Titan? Full story on our channel…'); end holds 0.15 (Titan), 0.29 (Kobe), 0.31 (Tacoma). The ending is the champion recipe, so this is a test, not a lesson; dd-end-on-fact tests what the ending says, this tests its length.
